entries.name: Big bluestem
entries.leaves: deciduous perennial; blue-green blades curing to tan
entries.flowers: tiny spikelets in 2-6 finger-like racemes ('turkey foot'), late summer
entries.voxel_shape: dense 1-3 m bunch of upright stems with three-pronged 'turkey-foot' seed heads
entries.notes: The namesake grass of the tallgrass prairie; forms waist- to roof-height stands that outcompete almost anything.

entries.name: Little bluestem
entries.leaves: deciduous bunchgrass; blue-green curing to russet
entries.flowers: slender spikelets on racemes, late summer
entries.voxel_shape: fine-textured knee- to waist-high tuft turning russet-red in autumn
entries.notes: The most widespread prairie grass in North America; the autumn russet colour is unmistakable on mixed grass plains.

entries.name: Switchgrass
entries.leaves: deciduous; upright blue-green blades
entries.flowers: airy open panicles of tiny spikelets, late summer
entries.voxel_shape: tall stiff upright column of stems topped by a cloud-like panicle
entries.notes: The bioenergy prairie grass; tolerates flooding and drought, stays green late, a staple of habitat seed mixes.

entries.name: Indiangrass
entries.leaves: deciduous; broad blue-green blades with hairy ligule
entries.flowers: large golden panicles with long awns, late summer
entries.voxel_shape: upright 1-2 m bunch crowned by a shimmering golden plume
entries.notes: One of the 'big four' tallgrass prairie species; the golden plume head shines in low evening light.

entries.name: Buffalograss
entries.leaves: deciduous (warm season); gray-green curly blades, stoloniferous
entries.flowers: bur-like female spikelets on short stalks, summer
entries.fruit: hard 3-4 mm bur containing 3-7 seeds, fall
entries.voxel_shape: tight low gray-green sod mat, a hand's height at most
entries.notes: Sod-forming shortgrass of the High Plains, co-dominant with blue grama; the grass bison and prairie dogs both crop.

entries.name: Kentucky bluegrass
entries.leaves: evergreen-ish perennial; canoe-tipped blades, sod-forming
entries.flowers: open pyramidal panicles, late spring
entries.voxel_shape: dense low sod of soft boat-tipped blades with airy seed panicles
entries.notes: The default lawn and meadow grass; spreads by underground runners to knit a seamless turf.

entries.name: Timothy
entries.leaves: deciduous; flat blades with bulbous lower stem
entries.flowers: dense cylindrical spike ('foxtail'), early summer
entries.voxel_shape: stiff upright stems topped by smooth sausage-shaped seed spikes
entries.notes: The classic hay meadow grass; short-lived so it needs regular reseeding, which is why old meadows are a conservation target.

entries.name: Common dandelion
entries.leaves: evergreen-ish; toothed basal rosette, deep taproot
entries.flowers: hollow-stalked yellow composite heads, spring to frost
entries.fruit: dry cypsela with white parachute pappus ('clock')
entries.voxel_shape: low toothed rosette with single yellow suns on hollow stems, later white globes
entries.notes: The first flower of any spring lawn and the last seed head of autumn; impossible to eradicate and happy to feed the player.

entries.name: Oxeye daisy
entries.leaves: deciduous; toothed spoon-shaped leaves on erect stems
entries.flowers: white ray florets around yellow disc, early to midsummer
entries.voxel_shape: slim upright stems tipped with classic white daisies
entries.notes: The midsummer meadow daisy; spreads by rhizome if mown at the wrong moment, a marker of old hay meadows under threat.

entries.name: Meadow buttercup
entries.leaves: deciduous; deeply lobed palmate leaves, upright stems
entries.flowers: glossy yellow five-petalled cups, late spring to summer
entries.voxel_shape: loose bushy sprays of shiny yellow cups swaying above lobed foliage
entries.notes: The glossy yellow sheen of damp meadow grass; toxic to grazing livestock (protoanemonin), ignore a field full of it at your peril.

entries.name: White clover
entries.leaves: evergreen-ish; trifoliate leaflets with pale crescent, creeping stolons
entries.flowers: white (pink-tinged) globes, spring to autumn
entries.fruit: tiny pod in the dried globe, summer
entries.voxel_shape: knee-high carpet of trifoliate leaves studded with white pom-poms
entries.notes: The welcome white fuzz in every lawn; fixes nitrogen, feeds bees and regrows from stolons no matter how it is trampled.

entries.name: Red clover
entries.leaves: deciduous; trifoliate leaflets with chevron, hairy stems
entries.flowers: dense pink-red heads, late spring to summer
entries.voxel_shape: soft clumps of pink magenta heads over hairy trifoliate foliage
entries.notes: The pollinator workhorse of hay fields and pastures; short-lived, so a good ley reseeds itself from its own seed bank.

entries.name: Common yarrow
entries.leaves: deciduous; feathery finely dissected leaves
entries.flowers: flat-topped clusters of tiny white (sometimes pink) florets, summer
entries.voxel_shape: soft ferny foliage with plate-like corymbs of tiny white florets
entries.notes: 'Soldier's woundwort' — the styptic of field medicine; thrives in poor dry soil where little else bothers.

entries.name: Wild carrot (Queen Anne's lace)
entries.leaves: deciduous biennial; finely dissected carrot leaves, hairy stems
entries.flowers: white laced umbels, usually one dark central floret, summer
entries.voxel_shape: lacy white umbels on hairy wiry stems, curls into a bird's-nest when ripe
entries.notes: Wild ancestor of the carrot; the one dark central floret is the old 'drop of blood' of folklore — a field of them is unmistakable in August.

entries.name: Chicory
entries.leaves: deciduous perennial; toothed dandelion-like basal leaves
entries.flowers: sky-blue strap-petalled heads that open with the sun, summer
entries.voxel_shape: sparse wiry stems starved of leaves, each tipped with an impossible blue star
entries.notes: The blue of road verges and dry meadows at 9 a.m.; by afternoon the heads are already shut tight.

entries.name: Field poppy
entries.leaves: deciduous annual; lobed hairy basal leaves
entries.flowers: scarlet four-petalled cups with black basal blotch, summer
entries.fruit: dry poppy capsule of seeds, late summer
entries.voxel_shape: thin hairy stems nodding with a single scarlet flame that opens at sunrise
entries.notes: The Flanders poppy; a buried seed bank that erupts whenever soil is churned — crop field, trench line, or roadside dig.

entries.name: Cornflower
entries.leaves: deciduous annual; narrow grey-green leaves
entries.flowers: vivid cornflower-blue ragged heads, summer
entries.voxel_shape: wiry stems tipped with electric-blue ragged buttons over grey foliage
entries.notes: The bachelor's button; a cereal-field weed now cherished in cornflower mixes for its impossible blue.

entries.name: Common sunflower
entries.leaves: deciduous annual; large rough heart-shaped leaves
entries.flowers: huge yellow rays around dark brown disc; buds track the sun, mid- to late summer
entries.voxel_shape: one towering rough stem, broad leaves, crowned by a dinner-plate yellow flower
entries.notes: North America's gift to the world; the wild form leans over the roadside while the crop form towers over the field.

entries.name: Cowslip
entries.leaves: deciduous; wrinkled basal rosettes of crinkled leaves
entries.flowers: nodding clusters of yellow bells with orange basal dots, honey-scented, spring
entries.voxel_shape: low crinkled rosettes with one nodding stem of yellow thimbles
entries.notes: 'Cow's-slip' — once trampled under cattle in the meadow; a keystone indicator of unimproved hay meadow, now rare in a modern scape.

entries.name: Greater knapweed
entries.leaves: deciduous; deeply lobed grey-green leaves
entries.flowers: large thistle-like mauve-purple heads, midsummer to autumn
entries.voxel_shape: loose upright stems bearing ragged thistle-mauve pincushions
entries.notes: The big scabious of dry banks and calcareous meadows; bees, bumblebees and fritillaries queue for it.

entries.name: Purple coneflower
entries.leaves: deciduous; coarse ovate rough-haired leaves
entries.flowers: purple rays drooping from a raised orange cone, midsummer to autumn
entries.voxel_shape: stout hairy stems, one per plant, topped by a purple droopy shuttlecock
entries.notes: The purple droop and orange cone that launched the herbal supplement industry; goldfinches harvest the seed through winter.

entries.name: Common milkweed
entries.leaves: deciduous; large opposite oval leaves, milky latex when broken
entries.flowers: fragrant globes of rose-pink star-like florets, early to midsummer
entries.fruit: warty pods splitting to release silk-floating seeds, autumn
entries.voxel_shape: stout unbranched stems with big opposite leaves and pink crowned flower clusters
entries.notes: The monarch butterfly's only nursery; the floss and latex tempted wartime inventors, but its real job is feeding caterpillars.

entries.name: Great blazing star
entries.leaves: deciduous; narrow grass-like leaves spiralled up the stem
entries.flowers: dense purple bottlebrush spikes that open top-down, late summer
entries.voxel_shape: single unbranched stem sheathed in purple fluff from midsummer upward
entries.notes: The upside-down spike: blooms downward, unlike every other spike in the field; prairie restorations plant it by the thousand.

entries.name: Compass plant
entries.leaves: deciduous; huge deeply cut rough leaves held vertically N-S
entries.flowers: sunflower-like yellow heads on rough 1-3 m stems, midsummer
entries.fruit: dry cypsela with two awns, autumn
entries.voxel_shape: first-year rosette of vertical cut leaves; mature, a 3 m stem with a dozen yellow suns
entries.notes: Settlers navigated by its N-S leaves; Aldo Leopold watched it die out as the prairie was ploughed. A must-plant for tallgrass theatre.

entries.name: Cup plant
entries.leaves: deciduous; opposite leaves fused into a cup around a square stem
entries.flowers: yellow sunflower-like heads, midsummer to autumn
entries.voxel_shape: tall square stems with leaves fused into stacked saucers, yellow tops
entries.notes: Birds drink from the water cups the fused leaves make; the whole plant is architecture you can walk through.

entries.name: Eastern pasqueflower
entries.leaves: deciduous; silky hairy finely divided leaves in basal rosettes
entries.flowers: nodding silky violet bell-flowers, among the first after snow, early spring
entries.fruit: feathery achene with long silky tails, late spring
entries.voxel_shape: tiny silky violet tulips peeping out of dry grass at first thaw
entries.notes: The first flower of the dry Eurasian grasslands, blooming while snow still lingers; a long-lived specialist of undisturbed steppes.

entries.name: Prairie smoke
entries.leaves: evergreen-ish; ferny silver-green basal leaves
entries.flowers: nodding claret-pink bells, spring
entries.fruit: achenes with long feathery styles forming 'smoke' plumes, late spring
entries.voxel_shape: low ferny tuft; first nodding pink bells, later a crown of pinkish smoke
entries.notes: The bells nod like a bobblehead and then explode into 15 cm feathery tails — the 'smoke' that set prairie seed heads alight in photographs.

entries.name: Pedunculate oak
entries.leaves: deciduous; rounded lobed leaves on short stalks, acorns on long stalks
entries.flowers: yellow-green catkins, spring
entries.fruit: acorn on a long stalk, autumn
entries.voxel_shape: broad dome on a stout furrowed trunk; the definitive lone tree of the lowland plain
entries.notes: The lowland giant of commons, hedgerows and drove roads; one mature oak feeds a thousand invertebrate species and a whole rookery.

entries.name: European ash
entries.leaves: deciduous; black opposite pinnate leaves, last to leaf and first to fall
entries.flowers: purple-black clusters before the leaves, spring
entries.fruit: winged keys ('ash keys') hanging in clusters, autumn
entries.voxel_shape: tall airy canopy of pinnate leaves on a smooth grey trunk; black buds in winter
entries.notes: Unbeatable for handles and oars; ash dieback fungus (Hymenoscyphus fraxineus) is erasing old lanes of them — model dead stags as a haunting.

entries.name: English elm
entries.leaves: deciduous; rough asymmetric toothed leaves
entries.flowers: reddish clusters before the leaves, early spring
entries.voxel_shape: broad wind-carved billow on a leaning trunk; often just a coppiced stool in a hedge
entries.notes: Dutch elm disease killed mature English elms wholesale; the hedgerow rows survive as root-sucker thickets — green above, dead below.

entries.name: Common hawthorn
entries.leaves: deciduous; deeply lobed glossy leaves with thorns
entries.flowers: white 'may' blossom in dense clusters, May
entries.voxel_shape: dense thorny dome or wind-shredded hedgeblock; full of white may in spring
entries.notes: The living fence of lowland England; a hawthorn hedge is a wall you can sharpen a scythe on, and a larder for thrushes in winter.

entries.name: Black poplar
entries.leaves: deciduous; triangular rustling leaves on long flattened stalks
entries.flowers: red male and green female catkins, early spring
entries.voxel_shape: towering wind-bent column of delta leaves over fissured dark bark
entries.notes: The riling giant of lowland river plains; old pollards and riverside lines mark where floodplain water flows.

entries.name: Fairy ring mushroom
entries.fruit: spores (white print) from lamellae under a tan cap
entries.voxel_shape: thin-stalked tan-capped toadstools tracing a perfect circle in the turf
entries.notes: The lawn-maker: rings widen a metre a year and can be centuries old; the darker arc of grass outside the ring is the fairy path.

entries.name: Meadow mushroom
entries.voxel_shape: small white button mushrooms with pink gills in the after-rain grass
entries.notes: The wild ancestor of the cultivated champignon; white cap, pink gills turning brown — but never pick without checking for deadly Amanita cousins.

entries.name: Giant puffball
entries.fruit: spores released as the brown interior bursts
entries.voxel_shape: a football-sized white dome sitting straight on the grass, no stem at all
entries.notes: Football dome on old pasture after rain; slice it white before it turns to chocolate dust — a meal of staggering scale from one body.

entries.name: Parasol mushroom
entries.fruit: spores (white print) from free white gills
entries.voxel_shape: tall snakeskin-stemmed mushroom with a broad parasol cap that flakes to brown
entries.notes: The snakeskin stem and mahogany-scaled cap are unmistakable to the initiated; beware the smaller toxic lookalikes before frying.

entries.name: Shaggy mane (ink cap)
entries.fruit: spores self-digested into black ink from the cap margin upward
entries.voxel_shape: tall white squid-like shaggy columns melting into black fringe by evening
entries.notes: The mushroom that dissolves into ink within hours of picking; pick white, cook tonight, and never near alcohol.

entries.name: St George's mushroom
entries.fruit: spores (white print) from crowded white gills
entries.voxel_shape: stocky white floury-scented buttons in rings on old pasture in spring
entries.notes: Named for St George's Day (23 April): the first true mushroom of spring, smelling of fresh flour on old undisturbed pasture.
